papers.abstract: To describe acute diencephalic syndrome (ADS) after superior transventricular surgery for giant pituitary adenomas with true third-ventricular extension, and to explore the association of ADS with extent of resection in a selected cohort. We retrospectively analyzed 40 adults operated on in 2015-2025 (23 total, 17 subtotal resections; 22 anterior transcallosal and 18 transcortical transventricular approaches). Postoperative AVP-D was distinguished from multidomain ADS, graded retrospectively according to the previously published four-stage framework. Final-stage agreement was reassessed independently in all 40 patients. Postoperative AVP-D occurred in all 40 patients; four had isolated AVP-D without ADS. ADS occurred in 36/40 (90.0%): 23/23 after total and 13/17 after subtotal resection (risk difference 23.5 percentage points; 95% Newcombe CI 3.5-47.3; two-sided Fisher exact p = 0.026). Stage III-IV ADS occurred in 9/23 versus 3/17 (p = 0.179). Independent final-stage agreement was 36/40 (90.0%; linear-weighted κ = 0.926). Five patients required mechanical ventilation, and two died. ADS was frequent in this anatomically selected transventricular cohort, but the operational definition is not specific for hypothalamic injury and the observational comparison is vulnerable to confounding by indication. The observed lower ADS frequency after subtotal resection is hypothesis-generating. Prospective multicenter validation is necessary.

papers.abstract: Second ipsilateral breast cancers present unique treatment challenges for patients that have formerly received breast-conserving surgery (BCS) with radiation therapy (RT). We utilized the population-based Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database to characterize temporal and regional trends in treatment selection for second breast cancer across the US. We identified a sample of 20,258 women diagnosed with second primary cancers between 2005 and 2022 who had previously received BCS with RT. Multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression models were fitted to determine associations between demographic, clinical, and geographic factors and the likelihood of receiving BCS with RT. In ipsilateral cancers, use of BCS with RT relative to mastectomy was significantly more likely from 2020 to 2022 compared to from 2005 to 2009 (odds ratio [OR] 5.16, 95% CI 2.99-8.90). BCS with RT was less likely in women with larger tumor size and hormone-receptor (HR) negative disease (OR 0.27 for tumors > 5.0 cm vs. tumors < 0.5 cm, 0.58 for HR- vs. HR+) Regional variation in treatment selection was significant for ipsilateral cancers, with an observed intraclass correlation coefficient within regions of 0.14 for relative usage of BCS with RT vs. mastectomy. Our findings quantify the extent of regional variation in treatment selection and describe key trends and characteristics of the patient population receiving radiation for second primary breast cancers.

papers.abstract: The aims of this project were to devise and benchmark internationally applicable quality indicators (QIs) for palliative radiotherapy (RT) "near end of life". To the best of our knowledge, this is the first multinational attempt at consensus on QIs for any palliative RT setting. Radiation and clinical oncologists with expertise in palliative RT, and cancer consumer advocates were invited to undertake a Delphi survey. The 30/30 invited panelists comprised 27 clinicians from nine countries and three consumers from XXXX and New Zealand, denoting a replicability in the upper range of "moderate" (defined as 60% to <80%). The panel initially agreed upon a definition of near end of life for patients undergoing palliative radiotherapy ("A state of irreversible functional decline from cancer and a short prognosis often measured in weeks or months"), and a timepoint criterion for benchmarking the subsequent QIs ("Patients dying within 30-days of starting palliative RT"). Nine candidate QIs were curated by the XXXX prior to the voluntary, anonymous survey which utilized an online platform (SurveyMonkey). Responses were appraised by an XXXX steering sub-committee, with 75% agreement defined as the iterative consensus threshold. The response rate for each of four Delphi rounds was 30/30 (100%). Supported QIs for near end of life patients relating to life expectancy documentation (2), waiting time for RT (1) and RT fractionation (2) were each benchmarked at ≥80%, with ≤30% for 30-day mortality. Additionally, the panel benchmarked conventional 30-day mortality (for all palliative RT patients) at ≤20%. Seven QIs were accepted and benchmarked, six for palliative RT near end of life, and one for all palliative RT patients. Real-world testing of the feasibility of these QIs and achievability of the benchmarks is required.

papers.abstract: This phase I/II single-arm trial assessed the tolerability and efficacy of stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) to all tumours plus intermittent androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) in patients with oligometastatic hormone sensitive prostate cancer (HSPC). Primary endpoint was the incidence of grade 3+ SBRT induced adverse events (AE's), including radiotherapy induced bone fractures. Secondary endpoints included failure-free survival (FFS), cumulative incidence of developing castration resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), and overall survival (OS). Eligible patients had synchronous or metachronous oligometastases (≤ 5 metastases, with ≤ 3 metastases in any one organ system) identified on conventional imaging. SBRT was delivered to all lesions, along with 1 year of ADT before stopping. Intermittent ADT (using 1 year cycles) was restarted when the prostate specific antigen (PSA) reached > 10 ng/mL, if new metastases developed, or earlier at the discretion of the physician. SBRT could be delivered to any new oligometastases that developed while off ADT in conjunction with restarting ADT. Eighty-nine evaluable patients with 171 metastases were enrolled. Median follow-up was 74.7 months. Thirty-three patients (37.1%) had synchronous disease presentation. Six patients (6.7%) experienced grade 3 AE's (5 patients with vertebral fractures and 1 patient with urinary tract obstruction). The 5-year cumulative incidence of restarting ADT and developing CRPC were 59.7% and 22.8% respectively. Five-year FFS and OS were 15.2% and 78.2% respectively. Higher PSA nadir after SBRT and 1 year of ADT was significantly associated with developing subsequent CRPC and worse OS. At time of last follow-up, 35 patients (39.3%) were alive with HSPC and not on ADT. SBRT and intermittent ADT for oligometastatic HSPC was safe and resulted in favourable long-term outcomes. A small proportion of patients did not progress in any way after SBRT and 1 year of ADT.

papers.abstract: Etentamig is an investigational B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) x CD3 bispecific T-cell engager, composed of a low-affinity CD3 binding domain, potentially reducing cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and infections, a high-avidity bivalent BCMA-binding domain, and retained FcRn binding supporting monthly (Q4W) dosing after a single step-up dose (SUD). We report long-term efficacy and safety from the ongoing, open-label, phase 1 (dose escalation/expansion; NCT03933735) and Arm A of the phase 1b (NCT05650632) studies of etentamig in adult patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, triple-class exposure, and ≥3 prior lines of therapy (LoT). In phase 1, patients received etentamig 60 mg Q4W or 40 mg Q3W, and in phase 1b, a SUD on Day 1 and 60 mg Q4W on Day 4. Among 146 patients (median age: 68 years; median [range] prior LoT: 4 [3-23]), median follow-up was 13 months (range: 1-48). Objective responses and ≥ very good partial responses occurred in 66% and 54% of patients. Median duration of response and progression-free survival were not reached. Pooled data suggest etentamig has a manageable safety profile, with Grade 3/4 neutropenia and infection occurring in 38% and 23% of patients. In phase 1b Arm A (n=23), overall CRS incidence was 30% (26% Grade 1; 4% Grade 2) with modified dexamethasone premedication and 1 SUD; median onset was 22.3 hours (range: 5.5-29.6) hours, with resolution in 20.7 hours (range: 1.8-131.7). Etentamig's molecular design may be associated with the observed clinical efficacy and tolerability while also potentially supporting extended dosing intervals.

papers.abstract: The prognostic significance of biopsy-to-radical prostatectomy (RP) ISUP grade discordance relative to final RP pathology remains unclear. We evaluated its association with prostate cancer-specific mortality (PCSM) and overall survival (OS). Using the SEER database (n = 30,303), propensity score matching yielded balanced cohorts for upgrading (n = 7,254 pairs) and downgrading (n = 3,671 pairs). Fine-Gray competing-risk regression assessed PCSM, and Cox regression assessed OS. Sensitivity analyses replaced biopsy ISUP grade with final RP ISUP grade in multivariable Fine-Gray models, and multicollinearity was evaluated by using adjusted generalized variance inflation factors. In biopsy ISUP-adjusted matched analyses, upgrading was associated with a higher risk of PCSM (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 2.15; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.49-3.11; P < 0.001), whereas downgrading was associated with a lower risk of PCSM (sHR 0.40; 95% CI 0.27-0.60; P < 0.001). Downgrading was also associated with improved OS in the original matched analysis (HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.66-0.96; P = 0.017), whereas upgrading was not significantly associated with OS. However, after replacing biopsy ISUP grade with final RP ISUP grade in sensitivity analyses, neither upgrading (sHR 0.73; 95% CI 0.45-1.19; P = 0.21) nor downgrading (sHR 1.46; 95% CI 0.87-2.46; P = 0.16) remained significantly associated with PCSM. Collinearity diagnostics showed no substantial multicollinearity. Biopsy-to-RP ISUP discordance was associated with PCSM in biopsy grade-adjusted analyses, but these associations were attenuated after adjustment for final RP ISUP grade. Final surgical pathology remains the dominant prognostic factor, and discordance should be interpreted as a prognostic/predictive signal rather than an independent biological driver.

papers.abstract: The prognostic significance of enlarged lateral pelvic lymph nodes (LPLNs) in patients with rectal cancer undergoing nonoperative management (NOM) remains unclear. This study evaluated whether pretreatment LPLN enlargement is associated with local regrowth or distant metastasis after NOM. The study retrospectively analyzed 77 patients with low rectal cancer who underwent NOM after radiotherapy-based neoadjuvant treatment between 2014 and 2025. Pretreatment LPLN enlargement was defined as a short-axis diameter of ≥ 7 mm on baseline magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Local regrowth-free survival (LRFS) and distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) were evaluated according to pretreatment LPLN enlargement. Pretreatment LPLN enlargement was present in 17 patients (22.1%). Among these patients, the median LPLN short-axis diameter decreased from 8 to 3 mm after treatment. During a median follow-up period of 55 months, local regrowth occurred in 15 patients (19.5%) and distant metastasis in 9 patients (11.7%). Pretreatment LPLN enlargement was not significantly associated with LRFS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.39; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.38-4.05; P = 0.587) but was associated with poorer DMFS (HR, 4.70; 95% CI, 1.24-19.01; P = 0.024). In an exploratory analysis treating local regrowth as a time-dependent covariate, pretreatment LPLN enlargement remained associated with distant metastasis (HR, 4.49; 95% CI, 1.20-16.84; P = 0.026). Pretreatment LPLN enlargement was associated with distant metastasis but not significantly associated with local regrowth in patients undergoing NOM despite substantial nodal regression after neoadjuvant treatment. Pretreatment LPLN enlargement may retain prognostic significance as a marker of metastatic potential in patients selected for NOM.

papers.abstract: Germline single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) are biomarkers that can be readily measured using DNA from peripheral blood or normal tissue. While SNPs have been associated with survival and cytotoxic chemotherapy response in several cancers, limited data exist on the clinical relevance of selected SNPs in oesophageal cancer (OeC) patients. DNA was extracted from normal tissue of 480 OeC patients treated with either surgery alone (S, n = 233) or chemotherapy followed by surgery (CS, n = 247) in the OE02 trial. SNPs in DPYD, OPRT, ERCC1, ERCC2 and XRCC1, GSTP1 and TS were analysed using MassARRAY, Sanger sequencing or gel electrophoresis. Associations with clinicopathological variables and overall survival (OS) were investigated. Selected SNP variants were associated with age, tumour differentiation, tumour regression and OS. The OPRT rs1801019 'GC' genotype was more frequent in patients aged >65 years (p = 0.034); the TS 5'UTR '3R/3R' genotype was more frequent in poorly differentiated tumours (p = 0.019) and the ERCC2 rs13181 'GG' genotype was nominally associated with improved tumour regression (p = 0.041). In an exploratory analysis, the ERCC1 rs11615 'CT' genotype was associated with improved OS (HR 0.80, 95%CI: 0.65-0.99, p = 0.040) in the whole cohort and in the subgroup of patients with adenocarcinoma treated by surgery alone. No associations were observed for any of the other SNPs. In the largest germline SNP analysis in OeC to date, ERCC1 rs11615 'CT' emerged as a candidate prognostic biomarker warranting validation in an independent cohort.

papers.abstract: CD8 T cells can make a decisive contribution to anticancer immune responses. While the glycoprotein CD101 is present on effector CD8 T cells, the signaling pathways driving CD101 expression and the outcome of CD101 engagement on CD8 T cells are elusive. Here, we show that the activation of TGF-β signaling induces CD101 on mouse and human CD8 T cells. CD101 expression on CD8 T cells was dependent on TCR signaling and TGF-β-induced Smad3. In multiple cancers, we found that mouse and human CD8(+) CD101(+) tumor infiltrating lymphocytes exhibited a resident memory phenotype, as illustrated by co-expression of CD69 and CD103. Accordingly, CD101-deficient mice featured accelerated tumor growth and were unable to respond to anti-PD-1 therapy. Altogether, these results suggest that CD101 expression on CD8 T cells has functional relevance and can be therapeutically exploited for anticancer therapy.

papers.abstract: Short preoperative immune induction could inform future breast-cancer trials, but it must not delay surgery. BreastVAX tested whether a single-dose preoperative regimen could be delivered within the planned surgical window while collecting safety and biological data. BreastVAX (NCT04454528) was a single-centre, open-label, phase 1b/2 window-of-opportunity trial. Adults with operable invasive breast cancer scheduled for upfront surgery received one 200 mg pembrolizumab infusion alone or with one 7 Gy tumour-directed radiotherapy fraction before or after pembrolizumab. The primary phase 1b endpoint was feasibility, defined as completion of assigned preoperative treatment within 21 days without delaying surgery by more than 14 days. Phase 2 had two descriptive interim reviews. In phase 1b, all six enrolled participants met the feasibility criterion. Across both phases, all 30 treated participants completed assigned preoperative therapy and underwent surgery without protocol-defined delay; median follow-up was 634 days (IQR 256-1120). Most adverse events were grade 1-2, with no deaths and no treatment-related grade 3 or higher events; the only grade 3 event was a surgical re-excision unrelated to treatment. Pathological and immune-correlative findings were exploratory and showed treatment-associated immune changes, including a neoepitope-reactive T-cell response in one responder. Pembrolizumab, with or without a single subablative tumour-directed radiotherapy fraction, was delivered within the preoperative window without protocol-defined surgical delay. Larger biomarker-informed studies should evaluate sequence prospectively, use endpoints suited to this short regimen, and prespecify harms monitoring. Philanthropic support to JCT and in-kind pembrolizumab supply from Merck Pharmaceuticals.

papers.abstract: HR+/HER2- breast cancer is the most prevalent molecular subtype of breast cancer, yet overall pathological complete response (pCR) rates after neoadjuvant chemotherapy remain low. BRCA mutations and homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) may sensitize tumors to PARP inhibitors through synthetic lethality. We investigated the efficacy and safety of fluzoparib combined with neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with HRD-positive and/or germline BRCA (gBRCA)-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer. This single-center, prospective, open-label, single-arm phase II trial (NCT07162051) enrolled women aged 18-70 years with newly diagnosed HRD-positive and/or gBRCA-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer. Patients received fluzoparib combined with docetaxel during cycles 1-4, followed by epirubicin plus cyclophosphamide during cycles 5-8. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving residual cancer burden (RCB) grade 0/I. Secondary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), pathological complete response (pCR) rate, and safety. Twenty-eight patients were enrolled between March 2023 and October 2025. Four patients (14.3%; 95% CI 4.0%-32.7%) achieved RCB 0/I, two patients (7.1%; 95% CI 0.9%-23.5%) achieved total pCR (tpCR), and six patients (21.4%; 95% CI 8.3%-41.0%) achieved breast pCR (bpCR). The ORR was 82.1%. Grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in four patients (14.3%). No treatment discontinuations, dose reductions, treatment delays, or treatment-related deaths were observed. The addition of fluzoparib to standard neoadjuvant chemotherapy did not improve RCB 0/I rates in HRD-positive and/or gBRCA-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer, although the regimen was well tolerated. Future studies should focus on gBRCA-mutated or higher-risk populations and explore optimized combination strategies, including anti-angiogenic agents. REGISTRATION CENTER, TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER, AND REGISTRATION DATE: This is a prospective, open label, single arm phase II clinical trial. Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov; Trial registration number: NCT07162051; Registration date:2023-02-21.

papers.abstract: Chordoma is a rare, locally aggressive bone tumor of the skull base, mobile spine, and sacrum that requires complex surgery, specialized radiation, and multidisciplinary surveillance. Centralizing care at high-volume, academic, or specialized centers may improve outcomes by concentrating expertise, but may also introduce access barriers. We systematically reviewed reported associations between centralized care and surgical, perioperative, treatment-related, and oncologic outcomes in chordoma. We followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception through November 5, 2026. Included studies evaluated chordoma patients and a centralization-related exposure, such as facility volume, academic status, or facility type. Where chordoma-specific data were not reported, authors were contacted and unadjusted chordoma-specific estimates were derived from patient-level data. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and findings were synthesized narratively. Of 1,790 records, 5 retrospective US registry studies met inclusion criteria. Centralization definitions varied across facility volume, academic status, and type. Centralized care was generally associated with greater surgery use and improved overall survival; surgery was more common at high-volume facilities (97.3% vs. 73.7%), and adjusted hazard ratios for worse survival at lower-volume or nonacademic centers ranged from 1.7 to 2.5 (derived from two non-overlapping cohorts). Patients at centralized centers traveled farther and were more often younger, privately insured, or metropolitan residents. High-volume and academic treatment settings were generally associated with longer survival in chordoma, supporting further study of specialized multidisciplinary care, though this advantage is inseparable from the access barriers shaping who reaches them. The registry evidence is limited by overlapping cohorts, differing definitions, and residual confounding, so it cannot establish the effect of referral or an optimal volume threshold. Future studies should adopt standardized measures of care setting and examine oncologic outcomes and access-related tradeoffs to inform models of care that can improve survival while minimizing disparities.

papers.abstract: Minibeam radiation therapy (MBRT) preserves normal tissue while maintaining antitumour efficacy, yet the mechanisms underlying this remarkable normal tissue tolerance remain poorly understood. Although adaptive immune responses have been implicated in the antitumour effects of spatially fractionated radiotherapy, their contribution to normal tissue preservation remains unknown. Here, we used a loss-of-function model to determine whether mature T cells are required for the expression of the long-term normal tissue-sparing phenotype associated with MBRT. Immunocompetent Fischer 344 rats and athymic nude rats received X-ray MBRT or conventional radiotherapy (CRT) at a mean dose of 30 Gy and were followed for up to six months. Long-term normal tissue response was assessed using complementary behavioural analyses, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and histopathological evaluation of immune infiltration, vascular integrity, glial activation and neuronal survival. Nude rats developed beam-path alopecia and skin lesions earlier than immunocompetent rats and showed a transient reduction in cortical CD31 staining at 7 days post-irradiation, indicating greater acute radiosensitivity without mature T cells. Beyond this early window, the long-term phenotype was comparable between strains: no MRI-detectable lesions, no neuronal loss and no sustained glial activation at 6 months. MBRT induced modest late reductions in exploratory behaviour and recognition memory in both strains, with no significant strain × irradiation interaction. Histologically, MBRT elicited a moderate and transient CD3+ T-cell infiltration that resolved within seven days, whereas CRT induced a stronger and more sustained inflammatory response. Mature T cells modulate the acute tissue reaction to MBRT but are not required for the long-term normal tissue-sparing phenotype. Within the sensitivity of this study, powered for large effects only, mature T cells are unlikely to be a major determinant of long-term MBRT tissue preservation, redirecting attention towards innate immune, vascular and stromal processes.

papers.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) affects millions globally, causing significant lifelong morbidity and early death. As childhood mortality is reduced and SCD patients are surviving to adulthood, increased risk of hematological malignancy (HM) is becoming evident. Risk of therapy-related myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS)/acute myeloid leukemia, following gene therapy or hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) is also higher in SCD. The specific pathobiology that predisposes to HM is necessary to address, since survival has improved and gene therapy and HSCT are being increasingly used. We modelled the increased risk of HM in humanized SCD mice, compared to age-, sex- and strain-matched normal counterparts. We serially monitored hematopoiesis in blood and bone marrow up to 1-year-of-age and performed highly sensitive, error-corrected deep sequencing of 450 MDS/HM-associated genes. Unlike controls, SCD mice showed an 'ageing-like' phenotype with premature development of myeloid-biased hematopoiesis and hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPC) mutational profile characteristic of aged mice/humans. Furthermore, a high proportion of SCD mice developed hematopoiesis with dysplastic features reminiscent of MDS morphology and higher clonal hematopoiesis burden. Imposition of regenerative stress by serial HSCT further increased HSPC mutational burden, resulting in evolution/expansion of clones harboring oncogenic driver mutations. Our study indicates that increased HSC regenerative stress, imposed either by chronic erythropoietic demand or via autologous HSCT in SCD increases the risk of developing clonal hematopoiesis and MDS-like features. Our study provides insights into a mechanism underlying increased risk of HM in this non-malignant hematological disorder, and suggests that early intervention with curative therapies may circumvent this risk.

papers.abstract: In the phase 2 FORTE trial, transplant-eligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma patients aged ≤65 years were randomized to (R1) carfilzomib-lenalidomide-dexamethasone followed by autologous stem cell transplantation (KRd-ASCT), twelve cycles of KRd (KRd12), or carfilzomib-cyclophosphamide-dexamethasone followed by ASCT (KCd-ASCT). Eligible patients were then randomized (R2) to maintenance with carfilzomib for 2 years plus lenalidomide until progression (KR) or lenalidomide alone until progression (R). With extended follow-up (median 99 months from R1 and 85 months from R2), KRd-ASCT significantly increased progression-free survival (PFS, median 98 months) versus KRd12 (median 70 months; HR 0.71, p=0.027) and KCd-ASCT (median 67 months; HR 0.66, p=0.006). A significant benefit in PFS2 was also observed versus both KRd12 (HR 0.65, p=0.02) and KCd-ASCT (HR 0.68, p=0.04) and in terms of overall survival (OS) versus KCd-ASCT (8-year OS: 76% vs 68%; HR 0.65, p=0.04). KR maintenance significantly improved PFS versus R (HR 0.67, p=0.02), with a time-dependent effect persisting up to two years after carfilzomib discontinuation; no differences in PFS2/OS were observed. KR significantly increased rate of measurable residual disease (MRD) conversion (sHR 0.47, p=0.03) during active treatment, and reduced MRD resurgence (sHR 0.53, p=0.001) versus R. Median duration of MRD negativity was 50.5 months in KR vs. 38 months in R arm. MRD-negative patients had significantly prolonged PFS with KR (HR 0.60, p=0.031); MRD-positive patients benefited from KR mainly during carfilzomib therapy (HR 0.46, p=0.05). The cumulative incidence of second primary malignancies was 6%. In conclusion, long-term follow-up confirms the high effectiveness of KRd-ASCT and KR maintenance. NCT02203643.

papers.abstract: Superior mesenteric artery (SMA) involvement is commonly considered a contraindication to surgical resection in locally advanced pancreatic cancer. The role of SMA resection during pancreatectomy remains controversial, with historical data suggesting prohibitive morbidity and poor survival. A systematic search of the literature was performed. Studies reporting on patients undergoing pancreatectomy with concomitant SMA resection were included. Primary endpoints were perioperative morbidity, 90-day mortality, and survival. Additional data on neoadjuvant treatment, patient selection, anticoagulation, reconstruction techniques, and oncological outcomes were also extracted. In total, 12 studies reporting on 320 patients undergoing pancreatectomy with SMA resection were included. All included studies showed a serious risk of bias and described highly selected patients. Concomitant venous resection was performed in 97% (n = 244/252) of patients and a total pancreatectomy in 63% (n = 173/275). Arterial reconstruction was achieved by graft interposition in 48% (n = 128/269), primary end-to-end anastomosis in 39% (n = 106/269), and splenic artery transposition in 13% (n = 34/269) of patients. Major morbidity and 90-day mortality were 31% (n = 88/284) and 8% (n = 27/320), respectively. Complications included post-pancreatectomy hemorrhage in 19% (n = 39/202) of patients and mesenteric ischemia in 3% (n = 6/202). R0 resection was achieved in 80% (n = 136/171) of patients. Median reported survival from surgery ranged from 8 to 20 months. The highest reported 5-year survival was 21%. Pancreatectomy with SMA resection is associated with specific perioperative morbidity and an 8% mortality rate. Since these outcomes were achieved by expert groups under highly selected circumstances, only implementation at high-volume centers with dedicated vascular pancreatic surgery expertise should be considered.

papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma is the most frequent extracranial solid tumor in children and the main cause of early childhood cancer deaths. Relapse occurs in more than half of high-risk patients despite rigorous multimodal therapy, and four-year overall survival in relapsed disease is approximately 20%. Anti-GD2 monoclonal antibodies and GD2-directed CAR T cell treatment have advanced the field, although neither has eliminated neuroblastoma's immune resistance. Current immunotherapy has three interrelated challenges. GD2 heterogeneity lets antigen-negative subclones escape and cause recurrence. Inhibitory cytokines, regulatory T cells, and myeloid-derived suppressor cells dominate the TME. MHC class I downregulation frequently renders traditional αβ T cell methods ineffective, even with the target antigen present. Gamma-delta (γδ) T cells offer a distinct mechanism. They recognize tumor targets without antigen presentation by sensing stress-induced ligands through NKG2D and DNAM-1 and phosphoantigens through butyrophilin proteins BTN3A1 and BTN2A1. This recognition holds regardless of MHC class I status. In conjunction with anti-GD2 antibodies, CD16 expression boosts antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. In neuroblastoma lesions, γδ T cells are the primary antitumoral fraction in tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte products, indicating compatibility with the disease's immune system. This study examines neuroblastoma immunotherapy failure mechanisms and innovative γδ T cell platforms, such as non-engineered allogeneic products, composite γδ T plus NK cell techniques, and CAR- and AbTCR-modified designs. A biomarker-driven patient selection paradigm and product standardization, in vivo persistence, and TME suppression are examined. NCT05400603, the first trial of adoptive transfer of ex vivo-expanded allogeneic γδ T cells in a population that includes pediatric neuroblastoma patients, is crucial for proving the mechanism.

papers.abstract: Chlorogenic acid (CGA), a naturally occurring polyphenol abundant in coffee and tea, has demonstrated antitumor activity in multiple experimental models. However, the cellular targets and mechanisms of CGA remain incompletely understood. Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) are key immunosuppressive components of the tumor microenvironment. Here, we investigated whether CGA regulates MDSC ferroptosis, thereby influencing tumor progression and antitumor immunity. We established MDSC-conditioned medium systems using tumor cells or CD8⁺ T cells as responder cells and evaluated the effects of CGA in murine models of lung cancer and hepatocellular carcinoma. Our results showed that CGA protected MDSCs from ferroptosis and reduced ferroptosis-associated lipid peroxidation. Consequently, conditioned medium derived from CGA-treated MDSCs showed a reduced capacity to promote tumor cell proliferation and migration and was less effective at suppressing CD8⁺ T cell function. In vivo, CGA significantly suppressed tumor growth in murine models of lung cancer and hepatocellular carcinoma and reduced the expression of MDSC-associated immunosuppressive factors within tumors. Flow cytometric analysis further revealed a lower proportion of BODIPY-positive cells among tumor-infiltrating CD11b⁺GR-1⁺ MDSCs in CGA-treated mice. CGA treatment also enhanced intratumoral CD8⁺ T cell responses. Mechanistically, CGA promoted NRF2 nuclear accumulation and increased GPX4 expression in MDSCs. NRF2 knockdown abolished the protective effect of CGA against MDSC ferroptosis. Together, these findings indicate that CGA restrains tumor progression, at least in part, by modulating MDSC ferroptosis through an NRF2-dependent mechanism. Collectively, these data identify MDSCs as a potential cellular target of CGA and support further evaluation of CGA as an immunomodulatory anticancer agent.

papers.abstract: Gastric cancer progression is closely linked to epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling and changes in the tumour microenvironment, yet biomarkers capturing these coordinated processes remain limited. We integrated transcriptomic datasets, machine-learning-based prioritisation, multi-cohort validation, single-cell analysis and functional assays to investigate ADAMTS2. ADAMTS2 was consistently upregulated in gastric cancer tissues and cell lines and discriminated tumour from normal tissue with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.945. Higher ADAMTS2 expression was associated with advanced clinicopathological features and poorer survival. Genome-wide co-expression and weighted gene co-expression network analyses identified an ADAMTS2-associated module strongly linked to EMT, TGF-β activity and invasion. These associations were consistently reproduced across three independent gastric cancer cohorts, with increasing ADAMTS2 expression accompanied by enhanced mesenchymal and invasion-related programmes and an opposing epithelial pattern. Single-cell analysis localised ADAMTS2 predominantly to fibroblast and myofibroblast populations. Across three cohorts, ADAMTS2 correlated positively with stromal and immune scores and inversely with tumour purity, while multi-algorithm deconvolution revealed concordant associations with fibroblast/CAF, macrophage and endothelial-cell infiltration. In AGS and HGC-27 cells, ADAMTS2 knockdown suppressed proliferation, colony formation, migration and invasion, increased E-cadherin, and decreased N-cadherin and vimentin. Stable knockdown also reduced xenograft growth. Collectively, these findings identify ADAMTS2 as a candidate biomarker connecting an EMT- and ECM-remodelling transcriptional programme with a fibroblast-rich, immune-remodelled microenvironment in gastric cancer.

papers.abstract: BRAF V600E-mutant colorectal cancer (CRC) has aggressive behavior and limited therapeutic options. We investigated whether dual-specificity phosphatase 4 (DUSP4) contributes to this phenotype and defined its molecular mechanism. DepMap and GEO data were integrated to nominate BRAF V600E-selective candidates. DUSP4 expression was validated in 30 paired tumors/normal tissues and an independent cohort (n = 326). Gain/loss-of-function studies were performed in HT29/RKO cells and xenografts. IP-MS, co‑IP, immunofluorescence, cycloheximide chase, inhibitor assays, and ubiquitination assays defined the mechanism. CD8+ T cells were analyzed by flow cytometry and chemokines by ELISA. DUSP4 was preferentially expressed in BRAF V600E‑mutant CRC and associated with nodal (P = 0.005) and distant metastasis (P = 0.019), and shorter overall survival. High DUSP4 independently predicted mortality [HR=2.102, 95%CI 1.395-3.165, P < 0.001]. Overexpression promoted proliferation, migration, and xenograft growth; knockdown produced opposite effects. Mechanistically, DUSP4 reduced PTEN protein stability and activated PI3K-AKT. DUSP4 recruited E3 ligase TRIM27, promoting K48‑linked polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of PTEN. TRIM27 manipulation partially rescued DUSP4‑dependent phenotypes. In vitro, DUSP4-overexpressing CRC cells impaired CD8+ T cell function, as evidenced by decreased expression of IFN-γ, GZMB, and CD107a. DUSP4 overexpression was associated with downregulated CXCL9/16, IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IL-2, and upregulated IL-10, effects partially reversed by PTEN overexpression. DUSP4 is preferentially expressed in BRAF V600E-mutant CRC and independently predicts poor prognosis. It promotes tumor progression via a novel TRIM27-PTEN-PI3K-AKT axis, and modulates the immune microenvironment by impairing CD8+ T cell function. DUSP4 may serve as a candidate prognostic biomarker and warrants further investigation as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.abstract: Cancer cachexia is a multifactorial metabolic syndrome driven by advanced malignancies and is closely linked to poor treatment tolerance and unfavorable prognosis. The neural-tumor-immune crosstalk within the tumor microenvironment is increasingly recognized as a key determinant of cachexia progression. Here, we show that gastric cancer (GC) patients with chronic stress (CS) exhibit poor outcomes that are closely associated with advanced N stage, perineural invasion, and cachexia. In vivo, CS accelerates GC growth and induces cachectic phenotypes, including gastrocnemius loosening, myofiber atrophy, and epididymal white adipose atrophy with browning. Mechanistically, CS enhances neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation and promotes sustained release of NETs-derived DNA, which drives both tumor progression and systemic metabolic wasting. NETs-DNA acts as a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) that persistently activates the cGAS-STING/NLRP3 inflammasome signaling axis in macrophages in a time-dependent manner, leading to amplified inflammatory responses that promote myocyte atrophy and impair lipid droplet formation. In parallel, CS strengthens neuro-tumor communication; nociceptive neurons sustain NETs formation via a feedforward CGRP-NGF signaling loop, whereas gastric vagotomy attenuates CS-induced NETs formation and consequently suppresses both tumor progression and cachexia. Importantly, combined inhibition of the CGRP/RAMP1 axis and the cGAS-STING/NLRP3 pathway produces synergistic suppression of GC growth and cachectic phenotypes. Collectively, these findings identify a stress-neuro-immune circuit that drives GC progression and cachexia, and highlight the CGRP/RAMP1 and cGAS-STING/NLRP3 axes as potential therapeutic targets.

papers.abstract: Chemotherapy resistance remains a major obstacle in the clinical management of gastric cancer (GC), driven largely by cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). CAFs activate the JAK/STAT signaling pathway in GC cells, promoting proliferation, migration, and resistance to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU). Fibroblast activation protein (FAP), highly expressed on CAFs but minimally in normal tissues, is an attractive target for molecular imaging. Here, we developed FAPtp-ICG, a near-infrared fluorescent probe comprising an FAP-targeting peptide conjugated to indocyanine green (ICG), for noninvasive visualization of FAP expression. We established CAFs-conditioned GC models with graded chemoresistance, in which FAP-associated fluorescence and FAP expression were positively associated with the degree of CAFs-mediated 5-FU resistance in the experimental models. FAPtp-ICG enabled noninvasive fluorescence imaging of FAP-associated stromal changes, allowing longitudinal assessment of treatment-associated changes related to CAFs-mediated drug resistance. Mechanistically, combination therapy with 5-FU and ruxolitinib (RUX) suppressed JAK/STAT signaling, alleviated chemoresistance, inhibited tumor growth, and restored drug sensitivity. Multi-omics profiling further revealed that RUX treatment was associated with transcriptomic and proteomic alterations in the tumor microenvironment, attenuating inflammatory signaling, immune cell recruitment, and extracellular matrix remodeling. By integrating a FAP-targeted optical probe with therapeutic JAK/STAT inhibition, this work demonstrates a theranostic strategy for assessing and overcoming CAFs-mediated chemoresistance in GC, supporting the potential utility of FAP-targeted imaging for longitudinal assessment of treatment-associated stromal changes.

papers.abstract: Venous congestion is increasingly recognised as a key determinant of organ dysfunction during acute kidney injury requiring continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Although the Venous Excess Ultrasound (VExUS) score is a promising bedside marker of systemic venous congestion, its dynamic evolution during CRRT remains unknown. We aimed to describe serial changes in VExUS during CRRT and explore their association with ultrafiltration intensity and fluid balance. MAVERIC was a prospective single-centre observational pilot study including adults undergoing CRRT for acute kidney injury. VExUS was assessed before CRRT initiation and after 24 and 48 hours. The primary objective was to describe temporal changes in VExUS using an alluvial plot. Patients were classified into three a priori-defined patterns of congestion evolution. Associations with net ultrafiltration (NUF) and cumulative fluid balance were explored. Forty-seven patients were included. Overall, VExUS grades decreased significantly during the first 48 hours of CRRT (p = 0.0048). Three a priori-defined patterns of congestion evolution were identified: persistently low congestion (45%, n = 21), resolving congestion (32%, n = 15), and persistent or worsening congestion (23%, n = 11). Patients with resolving congestion had the highest NUF rates (1.35 [0.85-1.66] mL/kg/h) and the most negative cumulative fluid balance (-36.7 [-74.6 to -21.1] mL/kg), with significant differences across groups (p = 0.003 and p < 0.001, respectively). Patients with persistent or worsening congestion had lower NUF rates. Serial VExUS assessment provides dynamic information on systemic venous congestion during CRRT. Three a priori-defined patterns of congestion evolution were associated with differences in net ultrafiltration and fluid balance. Serial VExUS monitoring may help identify patients with persistent or worsening congestion, raising the hypothesis that it could inform reassessment of decongestion strategies. Whether integrating serial VExUS assessment into individualised decongestive strategies improves renal outcomes should be evaluated in prospective interventional studies.

papers.abstract: WHO grade 2 meningiomas demonstrate substantial variability in recurrence risk, with longstanding controversies surrounding postoperative management. We performed a systematic review with individual patient-level survival analysis to characterize management and recurrence across three decades of published clinical experience, interpreted alongside contemporary observational and emerging randomized evidence. A PRISMA-compliant systematic review of PubMed, MEDLINE, and Embase was performed. Studies reporting patient-level data for WHO Grade 2 meningioma were included. Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox proportional hazards analyses evaluated progression-free survival (PFS). Overall, 203 studies comprising 640 patients were included; 337 of 629 patients (53.6%) experienced progression or recurrence. Subtotal resection (STR) was associated with greater progression hazard than gross-total resection (GTR; HR 1.87, 95% CI 1.42-2.45). Adjuvant radiotherapy (RT) following STR was associated with improved PFS (HR 0.34, 95% CI 0.21-0.55), persisting in landmark analysis (HR 0.34, 95% CI 0.20-0.58). Following GTR, the RT association was less definitive (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.55-1.26). Exploratory analysis did not identify a statistically significant difference in PFS between single-fraction stereotactic radiosurgery and fractionated RT (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.30-1.57). This patient-level synthesis characterizes management and recurrence patterns across published literature. Extent of resection remained a key branch point for postoperative risk, with adjuvant RT associated with improved PFS after STR but less definitive results after GTR. Considered alongside contemporary observational and randomized evidence, these findings highlight the value of refining individual recurrence-risk assessment and anticipated treatment benefit to inform more personalized postoperative management.

papers.abstract: Intra-abdominal candidiasis is frequent in critically ill surgical patients and is associated with high mortality. Whether empiric antifungal therapy improves outcomes after surgery for intra-abdominal infection (IAI) in critically ill patients remains uncertain. We conducted a retrospective single-center data warehouse-based cohort study of 1,061 adults admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) after surgery for IAI between 2018 and 2024. Patients who received systemic antifungal therapy within 24 hours after surgery were compared with those who did not. The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints were day-5 renal dysfunction, assessed by the renal SOFA component and the creatinine-based KDIGO stage, and the need for surgical reintervention. Adjusted analyses used propensity-score overlap weighting. Prespecified subgroup and sensitivity analyses used a Peritonitis Score ≥3, the identification of at least one organism in peritoneal samples, and a yeast-positive peritoneal sample. Empiric antifungal therapy was initiated in 46.0% of patients. Peritoneal sampling was available in 957 patients (90.2%); 21.4% had no organism identified and 25.2% had a yeast-positive sample. In adjusted analyses, empiric therapy was not associated with reduced 30-day mortality (OR 1.53, 95% CI 0.83-2.78), lower day-5 renal SOFA score, lower KDIGO stage, or fewer reinterventions. Findings were consistent in patients with Peritonitis Score ≥3, with at least one identified organism, and with a yeast-positive sample. ICU and hospital stays were longer in treated patients after weighting. Empiric antifungal therapy initiated within 24 hours after surgery for severe IAI was not associated with improved short-term outcomes. NA.

papers.abstract: To quantify heterogeneity in the treatment effects of first-line immuno-oncology (IO)-based combination regimens among patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (RCC) according to prognosis and potential effect modifiers and to assess which patients benefit most. Meta-analysis (preregistered in PROSPERO: CRD42023483638) including randomised trials underpinning first-line IO-based regimens recommended in the European Society for Medical Oncology 2024 guidelines using sunitinib as control, with mature overall survival (OS) data available as of November 2023. Individual patient data (IPD) were obtained for two trials and aggregate data for two others. Prognostic stratification was performed by the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium (IMDC) model and, for IPD trials, by the Clinical Prognostic Index in the Checkpoint Inhibitor era (CPI2) model. Effect modification by sex and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression was assessed. OS benefit was summarised as a hazard ratio (HR) and, in IPD, as the difference in restricted mean survival time (dRMST), and was pooled across trials using fixed-effects inverse-variance-weighted models. CheckMate-214, CheckMate-9ER, KEYNOTE-426 and CLEAR were included, totalling 3320 patients (IPD for CheckMate-214 and CheckMate-9ER; n = 1747). Among IPD studies, 42%, 32%, and 26% of patients had CPI2 favourable, intermediate, and poor prognosis, respectively. The respective pooled subgroup dRMSTs were 1.21 (95% CI = -0.82 to 3.25), 3.15 (0.50 to 5.81), and 7.36 (4.56 to 10.17) mo. Using all four studies, the pooled HRs for IMDC favourable, intermediate, and poor subgroups were 0.98 (0.81 to 1.19), 0.78 (0.68 to 0.89), and 0.51 (0.40 to 0.65), respectively. PD-L1 expression at 5% significantly modified the treatment effect. IO-based regimens showed highly divergent OS efficacy across prognostic subgroups, with no significant benefit among patients with a favourable prognosis and the strongest benefit in patients with a poor prognosis.

papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa), the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in men, shows only limited responses to conventional immunotherapeutic strategies, largely attributed to its immunologically "cold" tumor microenvironment (TME), which is characterized by myeloid cell populations and comparatively sparse infiltration of effector T lymphocytes. Neutrophils, the most abundant myeloid cells, are increasingly recognized as active regulators of tumor progression, yet their heterogeneity in PCa remains poorly characterized. This narrative state-of-the-art review addresses several questions: How do cellular and molecular cues in the TME shape tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs) in PCa and which mechanisms govern their plasticity? Do they have prognostic or even therapeutic significance and what are methodological obstacles in TAN research? A non-systematic peer-reviewed literature search across PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library was performed from 2000 to March 2026. Distinct TAN states are linked to CXCL1/IL-8-CXCR2-driven chemotaxis, IL-6 and IL-23-STAT3-mediated immunosuppression, and effector functions such as neutrophil extracellular trap formation. Spatial and single-cell analyses indicate that these functional states are shaped by local tumor-derived signals and therapeutic pressure, with potential impact on androgen receptor signaling and treatment resistance. However, neutrophil-specific biomarkers and clinically actionable targets remain limited, partly because neutrophils are technically challenging to capture in standard single-cell workflows. Collectively, state-of-the-art evidence positions TAN heterogeneity as an underexploited prognostic and therapeutic axis in PCa, one that merits further mechanistic characterization to translate TAN-based biomarkers and immunomodulatory strategies into clinical practice.

papers.abstract: For decades, ambulatory anesthesia pathways have commonly required a "responsible adult" before discharge after sedation or anesthesia. In practice, this requirement may function as a binary eligibility criterion based on a patient's social circumstances. However, the empirical evidence evaluating discharge without an escort remains limited and derives largely from observational studies. This Focal Point argues that carefully selected low-risk patients should be studied within structured alternative discharge pathways that preserve safe transportation, communication, observation, and rescue capacity. Such pathways should not permit self-driving or unrestricted solo discharge. The aim is to determine whether postanesthesia safeguards can be matched more precisely to patient, anesthetic, procedural, recovery, transport, and postdischarge risk while preserving conventional adult support for patients whose clinical circumstances warrant it.

papers.abstract: The highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) of glioblastoma (GBM) is particularly prominent in tumors exhibiting mesenchymal-like (MES-like) transcriptional programs and represents a major barrier to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). Integrating single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, we identified TAGLN2 as an immune-regulatory molecule preferentially enriched in MES-like tumor-cell states. High TAGLN2 expression correlated with increased tumor-associated macrophage infiltration and poor prognosis. Mechanistically, TAGLN2 drives immune evasion via dual pathways. Intracellularly, TAGLN2 directly interacts with HSPA8 and promotes p65 phosphorylation and NF-κB activation, with HSPA8 functioning as a downstream mediator. Intercellularly, TAGLN2 promotes ANXA2 stability and its enrichment in tumor-derived exosomes. Donor-cell ANXA2 loss-of-function experiments further showed that ANXA2 knockdown substantially attenuated the macrophage-remodeling activity, while recipient-cell analyses positioned STAT3 downstream of ANXA2, together supporting a TAGLN2-vesicular ANXA2-STAT3 signaling pathway. Direct EV intervention and donor-cell ANXA2 rescue in immunocompetent orthotopic glioma models further supported the functional involvement of this pathway in tumor progression and macrophage-associated remodeling. In an immunocompetent orthotopic glioma model, genetic TAGLN2 knockdown enhanced CD8-associated effector-marker signals and improved responsiveness to anti-PD-1 treatment. Through virtual drug screening, we identified Givinostat hydrochloride monohydrate, a histone deacetylase inhibitor prioritized by in silico prediction of central nervous system accessibility, as a candidate pharmacological modulator that directly binds TAGLN2 and modulates the TAGLN2-associated signaling network. Together, these findings support TAGLN2 as an important regulator of GBM immune remodeling and suggest a candidate combination strategy for enhancing responsiveness to PD-1 blockade.

papers.abstract: Proprietary processed EEG indices are less accurate in young children. We evaluated spectral edge frequency 95 (SEF95), a nonproprietary EEG index representing the frequency below which 95% of total EEG power resides, to establish target thresholds for varying anaesthetic depths during propofol anaesthesia in toddlers. Secondary objectives were to assess the relationship between SEF95 and plasma propofol concentration, and to evaluate airway reactivity during laryngoscopy. In this prospective study of toddlers aged 13 to 24 months, Dixon's up-and-down method and centred isotonic regression were used to determine the SEF95 targets for 50% (ED50) and 90% (ED90) probability of nonresponse to three clinical stimuli: pacifier placement (assessing consciousness), electrical nerve stimulation (nociception), and laryngoscopy (intubation readiness). Linear mixed-effects regression was used to analyse the association between plasma propofol concentration and SEF95. Among 51 toddlers, SEF95 ED50 and ED90 targets (Hz) were 21.8 (90% CI 20.8-23.4) and 20.3 (19.1-20.7) Hz for pacifier placement, 12.0 (10.8-18.3) and 10.4 (8.7-11.3) Hz for electrical stimulation, and 10.3 (4.6-11.8) and 4.4 (1.5-5.4) Hz for laryngoscopy. Each 1 Hz increase in SEF95 corresponded to a 0.21 μg ml-1 decrease in plasma propofol (r=0.46, P<0.001), as described by the equation: plasma propofol concentration (μg ml-1)=5.80-0.21×SEF95 (Hz). This study defined EEG SEF95 targets for loss of consciousness, response to noxious stimuli, and intubation readiness in toddlers aged 13 to 24 months. When combined with existing infant data, these age-specific SEF95 targets can optimise propofol titration and dosing accuracy during EEG-guided propofol anaesthesia in patients aged <2 yr. papers.abstract: Quantitative neuromuscular monitoring commonly uses acceleromyography (AMG) or electromyography (EMG). Acceleromyography requires unrestricted thumb movement, whereas EMG is independent of thumb motion. We compared the accuracy and precision of AMG and EMG responses after patients' arms were immobilized during routine surgical positioning. Patients undergoing general anaesthesia without neuromuscular block were enrolled. EMG and AMG monitors were placed on contralateral arms, and both arms were tucked under surgical drapes. The monitors simultaneously recorded train-of-four ratio (TOFR) after ulnar nerve stimulation every minute. Accuracy was defined as TOFR variability from the expected baseline value (1.00), and precision as consistency of repeated measurements, quantified by the coefficient of repeatability (CR). Failed measurements were defined as the absence of valid quantitative TOFR values, displayed as "0" or "?". AMG TOFR values were normalized to patient-specific baseline TOFR measurements for secondary analyses. Forty patients provided 3,733 TOFR measurements (1,879 EMG and 1,854 AMG). EMG was more accurate than AMG (mean EMG-AMG difference in absolute deviation from 1.0, -0.108; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.134 to -0.083; p < 0.001) and more precise, with a smaller CR (0.10 vs. 0.35; p < 0.001), including compared with normalized AMG (CR, 0.35). Device failure rate was lower with EMG than AMG (3.6% vs. 27.7%; p = 0.0003). Failures increased over time, particularly for AMG after approximately 45 minutes. EMG provided more accurate and precise TOFR measurements than AMG, including normalized AMG, with fewer failures, supporting EMG-based monitoring when upper extremity mobility is restricted. Clinical trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Database (Registration Number: NCT06805032, Principal investigator: J.R.R., date of registration January 28, 2025).

papers.abstract: The clinical application of precision oncology therapies is currently restricted to selected cancer cases harbouring highly specific mutations. Targeted therapies are typically approved for use in specific tumour types in which these alterations occur frequently. We aimed to systematically catalogue targetable alterations and genome-wide biomarkers across all solid tumour types to identify additional therapeutic opportunities. In this retrospective, pan-solid tumour analysis, for the primary cancer cohort, we used matched fresh frozen tumour and normal DNA samples and anonymised patient metadata from a discovery cohort of 11 013 tumours comprising 19 tumour types collected from 10 334 participants in the UK-based 100 000 Genomes Project (100kGP). Participants were recruited to this cohort through 13 National Health Service Genomic Medicine Centres or hospitals affiliated to the 100kGP between 2012 and 2019. For the metastatic cancer cohort, we used matched tumour and normal DNA samples and anonymised patient metadata from a cohort of 6016 solid tumours collected from 5658 patients from the Netherlands who contributed to the Hartwig Medical Foundation (HMF) database (accessed Aug 19, 2025). Snap-frozen tumour DNA and matched normal DNA from blood samples underwent whole-genome sequencing. Potentially targetable alterations, comprising (1) immediately actionable alterations, (2) investigational alterations, and (3) mutational signature-informed features, were sought in all samples. The primary outcome of this study was to assess the pan-cancer frequency and tissue distribution of potentially targetable alterations. Between July 1, 2025, and March 3, 2026, we analysed samples from 17 029 tumours from the 100kGP and HMF cohorts. Immediately actionable alterations were identified in 2081 (18·9%) of 11 013 primary and 1559 (25·9%) of 6016 metastatic cancers; a further 1204 (10·9%) primary and 867 (14·4%) metastatic cancers harboured investigational alterations or mutational signature-informed features. 2914 (51·1%) of the 5706 immediately actionable variants identified were found in tumour types where the biomarker is not approved by the US Food and Drug Administration. Although some immediately actionable alterations (including gene-fusion targets and MET exon 14 skipping variants) were restricted to fewer tumour types, most immediately actionable alterations (including HER2 amplification, RAS-RAF pathway alterations, IDH1 mutations, and DNA repair deficiencies) occurred across multiple tumour types, frequently beyond those for which matched targeted therapies are currently approved. Mutational-signature biomarkers of DNA repair or replication deficiencies were similarly observed across tumour types. Metastatic cancers, including rare and moderately rare tumour types and cancers of unknown primary, harboured a notably high prevalence and diversity of targetable events. Our findings support comprehensive whole-genome sequencing assessment of cancers irrespective of tumour type. Prospective clinical trials are required to establish whether therapeutic vulnerabilities identified by whole-genome sequencing can extend the effective use of targeted therapies beyond their current tumour-specific indications. papers.abstract: Uncertainty remains regarding the clinical advantages of sugammadex over neostigmine in older adults, particularly for recovery efficiency and postoperative outcomes. To compare the effects of sugammadex versus neostigmine on postoperative recovery and clinical outcomes in adults aged 60 years and older undergoing surgery. This systematic review and meta-analysis included eight randomized controlled trials. The primary outcome was postoperative residual neuromuscular blockade (PRNB). Secondary outcomes included post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) length of stay, hospital length of stay, time to extubation, hypoxemia, pneumonia, and postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV). Effect measures were risk ratio and mean difference. A total of 851 participants were included, and 50.2% received sugammadex. Sugammadex was associated with a lower risk of PRNB (RR 0.34 [95% CI: 0.18; 0.64]; p < 0.001; I² = 54%), with moderate between-study heterogeneity; however, the 95% prediction interval (0.11; 1.03) included the null value. Sugammadex significantly reduced PACU length of stay (MD -8.84 [95% CI: -12.18; -5.51], p < 0.001, I2 = 0%), hospital length of stay (MD -1.12 [95% CI: -2.01; -0.24], p < 0.01, I2 = 16%), and hypoxemia (RR = 0.61 [95% CI: 0.38; 0.97]; p = 0.04, I2 = 0%). No statistically significant differences were observed for the remaining outcomes. Sugammadex was associated with a lower risk of PRNB and shorter PACU stays compared with neostigmine. Although the primary analyses suggested reductions in hypoxemia and hospital length of stay, these associations were not statistically significant after the Hartung-Knapp adjustment. INTERNATIONAL PROSPECTIVE REGISTER OF SYSTEMATIC REVIEWS (PROSPERO): CRD420261376045.

papers.abstract: Biomedical research is constrained by the time and domain expertise required to analyze increasingly large and complex datasets. Here we present OpenScientist, an open-source agentic AI co-scientist designed to address this gap by investigating scientist-defined queries and generating verifiable, data-grounded analyses. OpenScientist was evaluated by domain experts across five biomedical case studies, completing analyses in minutes that otherwise would take months of human time and expertise. It accurately quantified Alzheimer's blood biomarker performance, generated a plasma proteomic survival model that predicted survival in a hidden-evaluation cohort, proposed a reproducible mechanism linking tau pathology to altered lysosomal acidification, generated multiple myeloma hypotheses validated in an external cohort with attenuated signal in randomized controls, and demonstrated concordance with an independent human analysis in a blinded, prespecified proteomic comparison. These results support the use of OpenScientist to assist biomedical data analysis in concert with human experts. To support research involving sensitive clinical datasets, OpenScientist can operate in a fully air-gapped environment using open-source models for inference. OpenScientist demonstrates that open, auditable, agentic AI can support real-world clinical research by researching the literature, generating hypotheses, executing analyses, and generating insights from complex datasets.

papers.abstract: Although induction chemotherapy (IC) in combination with concurrent chemoradiotherapy constitutes the standard treatment for locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LANPC), the optimal number of IC cycles remains undetermined. The 9th edition staging system provides a refined risk stratification framework. We aimed to develop a prognostic tool to stratify patients with LANPC and define the optimal number of IC cycles for distinct risk groups based on new staging. We analyzed 1216 patients with LANPC treated with IC and employed propensity score matching to minimize bias. Progression-free survival (PFS) was the primary endpoint, analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves. A recursive partitioning analysis (RPA) model was developed and validated for risk stratification. Survival outcomes and toxicities were compared across IC cycle groups. After a median follow-up of 56 months, 2- and 3-cycle IC yielded greater improvements in PFS compared with 4-cycle IC (p < 0.001). The RPA model incorporated 9th edition staging, pretreatment EBV DNA, and IC response, stratifying patients into three risk categories. For low-risk patients, 2- and 3-cycle IC yielded comparable PFS, both superior to 4-cycle IC (p < 0.001). In intermediate-risk patients, significantly higher 5-year PFS was achieved with 2-cycle IC than with 3- (73.4% vs. 56.2%, p = 0.014) or 4-cycle IC (73.4% vs. 47.5%, p < 0.001). High-risk patients benefited more from 3-cycle versus 2- (47.5% vs. 31.7%; p = 0.038) or 4-cycle IC (47.5% vs. 36.2%; p = 0.039). Overall, the RPA-based model effectively stratified risk, guiding individualized IC cycle selection. Balancing toxicity and efficacy, 2-cycle IC is optimal for the low- and intermediate-risk groups, while 3-cycle IC is preferred for the high-risk group.

papers.abstract: Central Asia is undergoing rapid epidemiological transition, yet internationally comparable assessments of cancer profiles in the constituent countries (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan) remain limited. We aimed to describe patterns of cancer incidence and mortality across the region and to project the future cancer burden through 2045. Cancer incidence and mortality estimates in 2022 were obtained for the five countries from IARC's GLOBOCAN database. Age-standardised incidence and mortality rates were compared by country, sex and cancer type. The future cancer burden was projected by applying age-specific cancer rates to population projections, assuming stable rates over time. In 2022, an estimated 92,665 new cancer cases and 56,110 cancer deaths occurred across Central Asia. Kazakhstan had the highest overall incidence and mortality rates, whereas the lowest rates across most major cancer sites were consistently estimated for Tajikistan. Breast cancer was the most common cancer among women, and lung cancer among men. The regional cancer profile was characterised by the coexistence of infection-related cancers alongside those linked to socioeconomic transition. Assuming stable rates, the annual number of new cancer cases is projected to increase by approximately 65%, reaching 152,000 by 2045, while cancer deaths are projected to increase by 73% to nearly 97,000 deaths. Cancer patterns in Central Asia suggest that regional cancer control planning should be nuanced to reflect each country's profile and resources, balancing prevention of infection-related cancers with early detection and effective management of common cancers associated with ongoing socioeconomic transitions.

papers.abstract: The expanding medical knowledge of tumour behaviour and advances in imaging, pathology, and therapeutic options require that TNM to be regularly updated. The 9th edition of the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) TNM Classification of Malignant Tumours was published in 2025 [UICC 9th Edition (2025)] to take effect on January 2026. Updates are performed in collaboration with the AJCC. Not all sites were updated in the 9th edition and were planned to be revised later. The update of Malignant Melanoma of the Conjunctiva is presented. The main changes are: T category is dependent on pathologic tumour thickness as pathological tumour thickness was a better prognostic indicator for T category than the previously used location-based classification, and for the first time Stage tables were developed and details are given below. To distinguish these new revisions from the UICC 9th Edition (2025), they will be designated as "UICC 9th Edition (Revision 1, 2027)" and abbreviated as "UICC-9.1.2027".

papers.abstract: The expanding medical knowledge of tumour behaviour and advances in imaging, pathology, and therapeutic options require that TNM to be regularly updated. The 9th edition of the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) TNM Classification of Malignant Tumours was published in 2025 [UICC 9th Edition (2025)] to take effect on January 2026. Updates are performed in collaboration with the AJCC. Not all sites were updated in the 9th edition and were planned to be revised later. The update of cancers of the colon and rectum is reported. The main changes are: clarification on what constituted regional or metastatic nodes (obturator nodes are regional for carcinomas of the rectum), that for low rectal cancer regional lymph nodes include superficial inguinal nodes, the inclusion of tumour deposit (TD's) - discrete tumour nodules in pericolic or perirectal fat as a stage descriptor, and subdivision of M1c into M1c1 (peritoneal only) and M1c2 (peritoneal with other sites). Stage was also updated and details are given below. To distinguish these new revisions from the UICC 9th Edition (2025), they will be designated as 'UICC 9th Edition (Revision 1, 2027)' and abbreviated as 'UICC-9.1.2027'.

papers.abstract: APOBEC proteins shape the somatic mutation spectrum of many cancers by binding and editing DNA. Modeling APOBEC-induced changes in cancer has been challenging due to the toxicity of these enzymes. Here, we overcame this barrier using a mutant form of APOBEC3A with impaired deaminase activity by changing arginine 128 to alanine (A3AR128A). Overexpressing A3AR128A in murine epithelium induced squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) in the skin, head and neck region, and cervix, mirroring the human disease spectrum. Tumor formation was further accelerated by concomitant Trp53 loss. A3AR128A cancers carried frequent alterations in the NOTCH and RAS-PI3K pathways, and recurrent mutations in genes encoding histone H3 were also observed. Cross-species analysis revealed how APOBEC accessibility influences cancer driver gene selection. A catalogue of 235,790 mutations was used to refine mutational signatures linked to A3A. These results shed light on how DNA damage from A3A contributes to tumorigenesis.

papers.abstract: Necroptosis is a regulated form of inflammatory cell death with context-dependent roles in tumor progression and immune regulation. However, the prognostic value and therapeutic implications of necroptosis-related transcriptional programs in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain incompletely defined. Transcriptomic profiles and clinical data for LUAD were obtained from TCGA and multiple GEO cohorts. Differentially expressed necroptosis-related genes were used to construct a prognostic model via LASSO-Cox regression, generating a necroptosis-related risk score (NRRS). Prognostic performance was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier analysis, time-dependent ROC curves, and multivariable Cox regression. A nomogram integrating NRRS and clinicopathological variables was developed and assessed by calibration and decision curve analysis. Functional enrichment, somatic mutations, tumor mutational burden (TMB), and neoantigen load were compared between NRRS strata. The tumor immune microenvironment was evaluated using ESTIMATE, ssGSEA, immune checkpoint analyses, and Immunophenoscore (IPS), with validation in independent immunotherapy cohorts. EGFR-TKI vulnerability was explored using pharmacogenomic prediction, external clinical datasets, CCLE analyses, and necroptosis inhibition assays in EGFR-mutant LUAD models. A seven-gene NRRS consistently stratified LUAD patients into high- and low-risk groups with significantly different survival across TCGA and GEO cohorts. NRRS remained an independent prognostic factor, and the NRRS-based nomogram improved individualized survival prediction. NRRS-high tumors were enriched for proliferative and genome-instability pathways, showed distinct mutation patterns, and had higher TMB/neoantigen load. Despite increased genomic immunogenicity markers, NRRS-high tumors displayed immune-depleted features, whereas NRRS-low tumors had higher immune infiltration, more favorable IPS profiles, and improved outcomes in immunotherapy validation cohorts. Higher NRRS was also associated with greater predicted sensitivity and clinical benefit from EGFR-TKIs, and necroptosis inhibition attenuated EGFR-TKI cytotoxicity in EGFR-mutant LUAD models. NRRS may be associated with EGFR-TKI vulnerability, immune microenvironment features, and potential immunotherapy responsiveness in LUAD. These exploratory results support further evaluation of NRRS as a candidate biomarker for therapeutic stratification.

papers.abstract: Acquired resistance to osimertinib remains a major challenge in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Using an osimertinib-resistant (AR) cell model lacking the on-target EGFR C797S mutation, we uncover sustained AKT phosphorylation under osimertinib treatment driven by insulin receptor (INSR) signaling. Notably, INSR-AKT activation is observed exclusively in AR cells, whereas parental H1975 cells fail to activate AKT even following INSR overexpression or exogenous insulin stimulation. Cholesterol depletion abolishes the INSR-AKT response in AR cells, indicating a lipid raft-dependent mechanism. Consistently, INSR localizes within lipid rafts in AR but not in parental H1975 cells. Proteomic profiling reveals the enrichment of lipid raft-associated proteins in AR cells. Among them, flotillin-1 (FLOT1) is identified as a key raft scaffold mediating INSR-AKT signaling and osimertinib resistance through functional shRNA screening. Co-immunoprecipitation and proximity ligation assay confirm a cholesterol-dependent interaction between FLOT1 and INSR. Functionally, FLOT1 knockdown disrupts raft-associated INSR localization, attenuates AKT activation, and reduces the IC50 of osimertinib in AR cells. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that lipid raft-dependent INSR-AKT signaling contributes to osimertinib resistance in NSCLC.

papers.abstract: Drug delivery systems (DDS) have become central determinants of therapeutic feasibility with modern medicines increasingly expanding beyond small molecules to biologics, nucleic acid therapeutics, and living medicines. As therapeutic modalities have continually diversified, delivery technologies, ranging from synthetic nanomaterials and molecular conjugates to biological carriers and hybrid systems have rapidly expanded. The increasing complexity of delivery strategies has thus necessitated conceptual frameworks enabling systematic comparison across platforms while accounting for engineering principles, biological barriers, and disease-specific therapeutic requirements. Accordingly, major delivery modalities now encompass lipid nanoparticles, polymeric and inorganic nanoparticles, targeted molecular conjugates, viral and non-viral vectors, cell- and bacteria-mediated delivery systems, extracellular vesicles, hydrogels, and device-assisted technologies. Although the mechanisms, clinical maturity, and therapeutic applications of these platforms differ substantially, they share common challenges associated with biological complexity, safety, manufacturability, and clinical translation. This review proposes a unified systems-level framework for contemporary drug delivery systems by organizing diverse delivery platforms according to carrier identity, payload class, and targeting mechanism. Engineering principles are integrated with a multiscale biological barrier framework encompassing systemic, tissue-level, cellular, and intracellular processes, thus providing a common mechanistic basis for comparing delivery performance across platforms. Clinical applications are further reorganized as per disease-specific biological barriers and delivery challenges spanning oncology, neurodegenerative, cardiovascular, metabolic, and autoimmune disorders, shifting the focus from platform-centered descriptions toward context-dependent therapeutic deployment. Emerging directions, including AI-enabled design, integrated delivery architectures, manufacturing scalability, and precision deployment, are discussed along with the shared translational bottlenecks that continue to limit broader clinical implementation. By synthesizing the engineering, biological, and clinical perspectives within a common conceptual framework, this review provides an integrated view of contemporary drug delivery systems and highlights the common engineering and translational principles facilitating the rational design, evaluation, and clinical implementation of future drug delivery systems.

papers.abstract: The Brazilian Society of Surgical Oncology (SBCO) developed evidence-informed consensus recommendations for intraoperative blood conservation and the rational use of blood components in surgical patients. Between June and December 2024, a multidisciplinary panel of 40 experts developed 48 clinical questions covering three perioperative phases: preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative care. This second article of the series addresses 16 questions related to intraoperative blood conservation. Expert working groups conducted structured literature reviews and drafted preliminary recommendations, which were subsequently reviewed by the project coordinators and submitted to an online consensus vote. Because high-quality oncology-specific evidence was limited for some questions, evidence from other surgical populations was considered when clinically applicable, with indirectness reflected in the wording and grading of the recommendations. An adapted evidence-classification system was used to determine the level of evidence and grade of recommendation. Intraoperative blood conservation requires an individualized, multimodal, and multidisciplinary approach. The selection of anesthetic, pharmacological, surgical, and blood-conservation interventions should consider the quality and directness of the available evidence, patient characteristics, surgical complexity, expected blood loss, and patient preferences.
